tasks.title: Set up dedicated worktree and opencode-loop queue
tasks.description: Create the dedicated worktree at /Volumes/SDD2T/obsidian-vault-write/custom-project/opencodian-view-single-responsibility-20260501, configure opencode-loop with a long-running tmux-backed execute profile, install blocking Codex review hooks, and initialize the lane status doc.
tasks.details: 1. Create the worktree: `git worktree add /Volumes/SDD2T/obsidian-vault-write/custom-project/opencodian-view-single-responsibility-20260501 main` (or appropriate branch). 2. Copy `.opencode-loop/` config from main checkout or create fresh with execute profile set to `tmux` and a long stale window (e.g., `--stale 3600`). 3. Run `opencode-loop hooks install-review` to install blocking Codex review. 4. Create `docs/status/lanes/t5-opencodian-view-single-responsibility/` with an initial status doc containing: current_task: 'setup', round: 0, last_commit: '', next_focus: 'identify seams', blocker_category: null, continue_loop: true. 5. Ensure `npm run verify` passes in the worktree.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify worktree exists and is clean. Run `opencode-loop status` to confirm queue is active. Run `npm run verify` to ensure baseline passes.

tasks.title: Identify and document safe seams in OpenCodianView.ts
tasks.description: Analyze OpenCodianView.ts using graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md and docs/modules/features/chat/OpenCodianView.md to identify the safest, low-risk slices that can be moved to existing adjacent owners. Document the candidate slices and their target owners in the lane status doc.
tasks.details: 1. Read `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` to understand current dependencies and ownership boundaries. 2. Read `docs/modules/features/chat/OpenCodianView.md` for documented seams. 3. Review `src/features/chat/services/`, `src/features/chat/runtime/`, and `src/features/chat/ui/` for existing owners that could absorb behavior. 4. Identify at least 3 candidate slices: e.g., debug/diagnostics render-support, child-session tree/context-usage, tooltip/copy support. 5. Update lane status doc with candidate list and target owners. 6. No code changes yet.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual review of documentation and code. No automated tests needed for this analysis task.

tasks.title: Move debug/diagnostics or render-support slice to existing adjacent owner
tasks.description: Extract one complete debug/diagnostics or render-support slice from OpenCodianView.ts into an existing owner in src/features/chat/services/ or src/features/chat/runtime/. Update docs/modules/ and refresh graphify.
tasks.details: 1. Identify the specific slice (e.g., a `renderDebugInfo` method or diagnostic logging). 2. Move the logic to the most appropriate existing service (e.g., `OpenCodeService.ts` or a runtime module). 3. Ensure the moved code is self-contained and does not create new dependencies on OpenCodianView. 4. Update `docs/modules/features/chat/OpenCodianView.md` to reflect the removal. 5. Update or create docs for the target module. 6. Run `npm run graphify:update:src` and `npm run check:graphify`. 7. Run `npm test -- --runInBand` on affected test files. 8. Run `npm run check:module-docs`. 9. Commit with message like 'refactor: move debug diagnostics from OpenCodianView to OpenCodeService'.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that existing tests still pass. Add unit tests for the moved behavior in the target module's test file. Run `npm run verify`.

tasks.title: Move child-session tree/context-usage slice to existing adjacent owner
tasks.description: Extract one complete child-session tree or context-usage slice from OpenCodianView.ts into an existing owner in src/features/chat/runtime/ or src/features/chat/ui/. Update docs/modules/ and refresh graphify.
tasks.details: 1. Identify the slice (e.g., methods that manage child session trees or context usage display). 2. Move to an appropriate runtime owner (e.g., `SessionManager` or `ContextService`). 3. Ensure no new thin wrappers are created; extend the existing owner's interface. 4. Update documentation for both OpenCodianView and the target module. 5. Run graphify update and check. 6. Run focused tests and module-docs check. 7. Commit.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify existing tests pass. Write unit tests for the moved behavior in the target module. Run `npm run verify`.

tasks.title: Move tooltip/copy or assistant/user render-support slice to existing adjacent owner
tasks.description: Extract one complete tooltip/copy or assistant/user render-support slice from OpenCodianView.ts into an existing owner in src/features/chat/ui/ or src/features/chat/services/. Update docs/modules/ and refresh graphify.
tasks.details: 1. Identify the slice (e.g., tooltip rendering logic or copy-to-clipboard handler). 2. Move to an appropriate UI or service owner (e.g., `ChatUI` or `ClipboardService`). 3. Ensure the moved code does not increase OpenCodianView's responsibilities. 4. Update docs and run graphify. 5. Run tests and module-docs check. 6. Commit.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify existing tests pass. Add unit tests for the moved behavior. Run `npm run verify`.

tasks.title: Move activation/sync/question/todo/background-task host assembly slice (if safe)
tasks.description: If feasible, extract one complete activation/sync/question/todo/background-task host assembly slice from OpenCodianView.ts into an existing owner, ensuring it reduces view-owned callback surface without introducing a thin bridge chain. Update docs/modules/ and refresh graphify.
tasks.details: 1. Evaluate if any activation/sync/question/todo/background-task slice can be moved without creating a thin bridge. 2. If yes, move to an appropriate runtime owner (e.g., `TaskService` or `SyncManager`). 3. Ensure the target owner already exists and is not a new thin wrapper. 4. Update docs and run graphify. 5. Run tests and module-docs check. 6. Commit. If not feasible, skip and document reasoning in lane status doc.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify existing tests pass. Add unit tests for the moved behavior. Run `npm run verify`.

tasks.title: Update lane status doc and refresh graphify after each task
tasks.description: After each source task (17-20), update the lane status doc with current task, round, last commit, next focus, blocker category if any, and whether the loop should continue. Also refresh graphify-out/ after any src/ changes.
tasks.details: 1. After each commit from tasks 17-20, run `npm run graphify:update:src` and `npm run check:graphify`. 2. Update `docs/status/lanes/t5-opencodian-view-single-responsibility/status.md` with: current_task (the task just completed), round (increment), last_commit (SHA), next_focus (next task ID or 'done'), blocker_category (if any), continue_loop (true unless blocker). 3. Commit the status update. 4. This task runs iteratively after each source task; it is listed as a single task but executed multiple times.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that graphify-out/ is updated and consistent. Check that status doc is accurate.

tasks.title: Run full verification and finalize queue
tasks.description: Run the full verification gate (`npm run verify`) after all source tasks are complete. If any failures occur, address them as fallout. Update the lane status doc to mark the queue as complete or blocked. Record a rolling status checkpoint.
tasks.details: 1. Run `npm run verify` in the worktree. 2. If failures occur, fix them (limited to test adjustments or minor fallout; no new feature work). 3. Update lane status doc: set continue_loop to false, record final commit, and note any blockers. 4. Ensure all docs/modules/ are up-to-date. 5. Commit final status. 6. Optionally, push the worktree branch for review.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run verify` and ensure zero failures. Run `npm run check:module-docs` and `npm run check:graphify` as part of verify.
